source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 11.

sections.heading: 1. Light Travels in a Straight Line
points: **Light travels in a straight line** (rectilinear propagation).
Objects are grouped by how light passes: **transparent** (light passes fully — glass), **translucent** (partly — butter paper), **opaque** (does not pass — wood, metal).
We **see** an object when light from it enters our eyes.

sections.heading: 2. Shadows
points: A **shadow** forms when an **opaque object** blocks light — proof that light travels straight.
A shadow needs a **source of light, an opaque object, and a screen**.
A shadow is **always dark** (shows only shape/outline, not colour); its **size changes** with the object's distance from the source/screen.
A **pinhole camera** forms an **inverted image** — another proof light travels straight.

sections.heading: 3. Reflection
points: **Reflection** = the bouncing back of light from a **shiny/polished surface** (like a mirror).
A **plane mirror** forms an image that is **virtual, erect, of the same size**, as far behind as the object is in front, and **laterally inverted** (left↔right reversed).
**Lateral inversion** is why AMBULANCE is written reversed so it reads correctly in a mirror.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Light travels in straight lines; transparent (glass) / translucent (butter paper) / opaque (wood).
Shadow: needs source + opaque object + screen; always dark; shows shape not colour.
Pinhole camera gives an inverted image (light travels straight).
Plane mirror image: virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **shadow shows only the outline** (shape), never the colour of the object.
A **translucent** object lets light pass **partly** (between transparent and opaque).
A plane-mirror image is **laterally inverted** (left↔right), not upside-down.
A **pinhole camera** forms an **inverted** image because light travels straight.
